en: The Ritual for Cultivating and Realizing the Vows and Practices of Samantabhadra from the Avataṃsaka Sūtra, Compiled by the Śramaṇa Jingyuan of Jinshui, a Transmitter of the Huayan Teachings and Contemplations of the Song Dynasty.
Part One: A General Introduction to the Origins.
Section Two: Encouraging Cultivation for Benefit.
Section Three: Discerning the Vessel.

Regarding those capable of entering the ritual arena (*maṇḍala*) to perform prostrations and repentance, there are briefly three types: first, those who practice and enter realization; second, those who extinguish karma.
Accomplishing faith. Third, perfuming the seeds and forming a karmic connection.
Fourth, rebuking and abandoning the hindrance of desire;
there are five grains of desire, namely: form, sound, fragrance, taste, and touch. These five constants can delude ordinary people, causing them to give rise to [afflictions].

Attachment causes one to lose the resolve for the Path. Therefore, those who wish to perform rituals of repentance and cultivate meditative observation (*dhyāna-vipaśyanā*) must reprove [these hindrances] so that the mind never again becomes bound by them.
There are five such grains: first, sensual desire; second, ill-will; third, sloth and torpor; fourth, restlessness and remorse; and fifth, doubt. These five—
When it arises, it covers over the mind and wisdom; therefore, it must be abandoned forever and not retained in the mind.
Resolutely resolve to advance in cultivation:
fifth, purifying the site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*); sixth...
Adorn the altar, purify the robes, and cleanse the body and mind.

Having thus requested the sages and worthies, the seventh practitioner enters the ritual arena for the first time. Reciting the name of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, they circumambulate the site once and proceed before the Dharma seat.

Having spread out the *niṣīdana* mat, one should stand upright with the body straight and palms joined. One should first cultivate thoughts of loving-kindness toward all sentient beings, vowing to deliver and uplift them all.
Next, one should give rise to a heart of profound reverence and respectfully invoke the Triple Gem. Holding an incense burner in hand, one burns various sublime incenses.
The presiding master then says:
With all reverence and single-minded devotion, pay homage.

In the Flower Treasury World (*kusumatalagarbha-lokadhātu*), within the realm of the Imperial Net (*indrajāla*), to the Three Jewels who eternally abide throughout the entire *dharmadhātu* (having completed one prostration, kneel with the right knee on the ground, burn incense, scatter flowers, maintain single-minded right mindfulness, and vocally recite the names of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, making individual petitions; do not be disrespectful or distracted).
With single-minded devotion, we entreat you: when the ten bodies were first perfected and true awakening was initially attained, without leaving Jambudvīpa, you ascended to the heavens;
your inexhaustible clouds of bodies pervade the entire dharma-realm. Great Vairocana Buddha (three entreaties and one prostration; hereafter, follow this pattern).

With single-minded devotion, he made his invocation; the Buddha appeared radiantly in response. In the Land of Ultimate Bliss, the universal cause was fully perfected; amidst the lotuses, Amitābha Buddha bestowed upon him the prediction of enlightenment.

With single-minded devotion, I make this invocation: In the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, the Buddhas from the ten directions assemble like clouds; they utter words of praise for meditative concentration and manifest themselves before him, all bearing the same name, Dharmamati, within the Forest of Merit. All these Buddhas—
With single-minded devotion, I extend this invitation to all the Buddhas, as numerous as atoms, within the Indra-net worlds of the Flower Treasury World (*kusumatalagarbhadhātu*).
With single-minded devotion, I invite the *Mahāvaipulya-buddhāvataṃsaka-sūtra*, the fundamental wheel of Dharma, vast and all-encompassing, profound and harmonious,
the inconceivable and perfectly integrated Jewel of the Dharma.
With single-minded devotion, we entreat you to accept the *Śākyamuni-bhāṣita-parivāra-sūtra* and other such scriptures, as numerous as the atoms within the buddha-fields of the ten directions—
the entire *sūtra-piṭaka* of all dharma-gates.

With single-minded devotion, we make this invocation: At the primary site of enlightenment within the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, where he first attained perfect awakening, the Buddha—the sovereign of the assembly of the fruition of Buddhahood, presiding over both the primary and secondary retributions—is accompanied by Samantabhadra Bodhisattva. Simultaneously, they gather like clouds, pervading the entire dharma-realm, together with all the great Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas.

With single-minded devotion, we make this invocation: In the second chapter of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, the Assembly on Questions and Answers Concerning the Ten Faiths held in the Hall of Universal Radiance,
the presiding hosts are the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, the Bodhisattva Awakening Chief, the Bodhisattva Wealth Chief, the Bodhisattva Jewel Chief,
the Bodhisattva Virtue Chief, the Bodhisattva Eye Chief, the Bodhisattva Diligence Chief, the Bodhisattva Dharma Chief, and the Bodhisattva Wisdom Chief.
Sā. The Bodhisattvas, O Worthy Leader, gathered together simultaneously, pervading the entire Dharma-realm. All these great Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas, with one mind, made this request:
[to the Lord] Dharmamati, the presiding host of the "Ten Abodes" assembly in the third chapter of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, held in the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven Palace.

The Bodhisattvas— Sarvajñāna-bodhisattva, Vijñāna-bodhisattva, Guṇajñāna-bodhisattva, Vīryajñāna-bodhisattva, Sudhī-bodhisattva, Prajñā-bodhisattva, Tattvajñāna-bodhisattva, Anuttarajñāna-bodhisattva,
and Dṛḍhajñāna-bodhisattva— assembled simultaneously, pervading the entire dharma-realm; these great bodhisattva-mahāsattvas...
O Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, with single-minded devotion, I entreat you: in the fourth assembly of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, held in the Night-Heaven (Yāma) Palace, may the Lord of the Assembly,

the Bodhisattva Forest of Merit (Guṇakānanavatī), the Bodhisattva Forest of Wisdom (Jñānakānanavatī), the Bodhisattva Forest of Victory (Jayakānanavatī), the Bodhisattva Forest of Fearlessness (Abhayakānanavatī), and the Bodhisattva Forest of Shame and Remorse (Hrīvyapatrāpyakānanavatī) [be present].
The Bodhisattvas— Vīra-vana Bodhisattva, Bala-vana Bodhisattva, Carya-vana Bodhisattva, Bodhi-vana Bodhisattva, and Jñāna-vana Bodhisattva—
assembled simultaneously, pervading the entire Dharma-realm, together with all these great Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas.
With single-minded devotion, we offer this invocation: To the Bodhisattvas who preside over the assembly of the Ten Dedications in the fifth chapter of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*,
held within the Tuṣita Heaven Palace— Vajradhvaja Bodhisattva, Sthiradhvaja Bodhisattva, Parākramadhvaja Bodhisattva, Prabhādhvaja Bodhisattva,
Jñānadhvaja Bodhisattva, Ratnadhvaja Bodhisattva, Vīryadhvaja Bodhisattva, Vimaladhvaja Bodhisattva, and Tārakadhvaja Bodhisattva.

The Bodhisattva Sovereign Banner and the Bodhisattva Dharma Banner assembled simultaneously, pervading the entire dharma-realm. All these great Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, with one mind, made this request:
the sixth chapter of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, the dialogue on the Ten Stages in the Palace of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven.

The presiding host was the Bodhisattva Vimukticandra, together with the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha and others; they gathered simultaneously in clouds, pervading the entire dharma-realm, along with all the great Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas.
With single-minded devotion, we offer this invocation: In the seventh assembly of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, held in the Hall of Universal Radiance,
the principal figures— the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, the Bodhisattva Samantanetra, the Bodhisattva Cittarāja,
the Bodhisattva Nīlotpalagarbha, the Bodhisattva Ratnapāṇi, and the Bodhisattva Tathāgatagotra-samudgata-vimalaguṇa— gathered together simultaneously, pervading all places.
In the eighth assembly of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, held at the Hall of Universal Radiance within the Dharma-realm, the great Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas with one mind made this solemn request:

that the presiding masters of the assembly for the questions and answers on entrusting the Dharma and advancing in practice— namely, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra and the Bodhisattva Samantamati— should gather together like clouds from all directions.
The great Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas throughout the entire Dharma-realm,
with one mind, reverently entreat the Lord of the Assembly who realized and entered the Dharma-realm in the ninth chapter of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, "In the Jeta Grove."
Before the Tathāgata were the two great Bodhisattvas Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra; the presiding masters of the final assembly:
the Bodhisattva Great Spiritual Friend Wondrous Chief of the Dharma-gate of the Ten Faiths; the ten spiritual friends including the Venerable Cloud of Virtue of the Dharma-gate of the Ten Abidings;
the ten spiritual friends including the Bhikṣu Good Vision of the Dharma-gate of the Ten Practices; and [the ten spiritual friends of] the Ten Dedications...
The Dharma-gate of the Blue Lotus: the ten spiritual friends beginning with the Elder;
the Dharma-gate of the Ten Stages: the ten spiritual friends beginning with the Night Goddess Vasanti; the Dharma-gate of Equal Enlightenment:
the eleven spiritual friends beginning with the Noble Lady Māyā; and the Dharma-gate of Gathering Virtues to Accomplish Causes: the Great Spiritual Friend Maitreya Bodhisattva.
The great spiritual friend Bodhisattva Wondrous Virtue of the Dharma Door of Non-dual Wisdom-Illumination;
the great spiritual friend Bodhisattva Samantabhadra of the Dharma Door of Manifesting Causes and Vastness; and bodhisattva-mahāsattvas as numerous as atoms.

With single-minded devotion, we invoke the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, who is perfectly pervasive and unimpeded, dwelling throughout the ten directions upon Mount Potalaka, whose great compassion universally delivers all beings.

With single-minded devotion, I entreat you: Maitreya Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, the Compassionate Honored One who dwells in the next position of succession, residing within the Adorned Pavilion of Vairocana.

With single-minded devotion, I entreat you: You who, at the assembly of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, gave rise to the bodhicitta and vowed to accomplish [the goal] in a single lifetime by seeking the various paths of the south.
The supreme and perfect recipient, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Sudhana, with single-minded devotion made this request.
From within the Bodhi tree, upon the lion throne, there appeared from between his eyebrows as many [emanations] as there are atoms in a Buddha-field.
In the ocean-like assembly of the Avataṃsaka, within the Flower Treasury World, layer upon layer, infinitely and inexhaustibly,
are all the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas of the ten directions and the three periods of time.
With one mind, we reverently entreat you: the five hundred śrāvakas headed by Śāriputra and the six thousand bhikṣus within the final assembly at the Jeta Grove;
and all the śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and noble saṅgha from all the buddha-fields of the ten directions.
With single-minded devotion, I invoke the Vajrapāṇi deities from the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, the deities of the body, the deities of the feet,

the deities of the site of enlightenment, the deity of the city, the deity of the earth, the deity of the mountains, the deity of the forests, the deity of medicinal herbs, the deity of crops, the deity of rivers,

the deity of the oceans, the deity of water, the deity of fire, the deity of wind, the deity of space, the deity of the directions, the deity of night, and the deity of day, as well as the eight classes of beings, including devas and nāgas. Thus I pray.
Brahmā Devānām-Indra, the immeasurable devas, the sons of the Sun and Moon, and the entire assembly of noble ones—(this section is for invitation only;
one should not prostrate. For laypeople, there is no such restriction). Having thus completed the sequence of invitations, one then makes this declaration aloud:
I only pray that the World-Honored One Vairocana, Amitābha Buddha, all the Buddhas gathered from the ten directions,
and the Buddhas as numerous as the atoms within the Flower Treasury World, out of your great kindness and great compassion, will accept my invitation, come to this site of practice,
and bear witness to my repentance.

The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, the Dharma-gate of perfect interfusion and non-obstruction: I pray that every passage may accord with my intent and every phrase may harmonize with my mind, so that it may manifest within this site of enlightenment and bear witness to my repentance.
Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva, Dharmamati Bodhisattva, and all the great Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas throughout the Avataṃsaka Sūtra—
endowed with great loving-kindness and great compassion— accept my invitation to come to this site of practice and bear witness to my repentance.
Śāriputra and the five hundred śrāvakas, along with six thousand bhikṣus— all of whom are endowed with compassion—
have accepted my invitation and come to this site of practice to bear witness to my repentance.
May the eight classes of devas and nāgas, the Vajrapāṇi deities, the deities who preside over space, and even the presiding deities throughout all worlds,
all give rise to compassion, accept my invitation, come to this place of practice, and bear witness to my repentance.

May this assembly of noble ones all bear witness: today, for the sake of all sentient beings in the six realms throughout the ten directions, I wish to practice the unsurpassed Bodhi of the One Vehicle and destroy all heavy sins that obstruct the Path.

May I attain the Sea-Seal Samādhi (Sāgaramudrā-samādhi) and pervade the entire Dharma-realm with my body. For several tens of days, I shall practice with single-minded diligence, as prescribed in the sutras.

Thus it is said regarding the practice of cultivation: "I pray that all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, and the Celestial Teacher Samantabhadra, by the power of their original vows, will accept my repentance, cause my practice to become resolute, destroy all karmic obstacles of sin, and bring the Dharma-gate before me, just as described in the sutras.

(The practitioner should, by means of their own wisdom-power, express the intent of their petition to the Buddhas; thereafter, they should offer praise and offerings, circumambulate while reciting the sutra, take the three refuges three times, and exit by circling to the right, waiting for the first light of day.)

Only after this division may one properly cultivate the Ten Practices. The method for this formal cultivation remains the same as before: invoke the name of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva and arise from a state of total reverence toward all things; however, the act of formal petition is omitted.
The eighth of the ten practices of correct cultivation:

First, paying homage to all Buddhas. (All its benefits include the ability to sever the obstacles of the seven, nine, and ten types of pride, and the attainment of a body of noble dignity and sovereignty, adorned with the perfection of the eighty-four thousand marks and signs.)
With single-minded reverence, I pay homage. When the ten bodies were first perfected and true awakening was initially attained, without departing from Jambudvīpa, you ascended to the heavens;
your inexhaustible clouds of bodies pervade the entire Dharma-realm. Great Vairocana Buddha (three prostrations).

With single-minded reverence, I pay homage. The world of Ultimate Bliss manifests radiantly; it universally gathers those with perfected causes, bestowing predictions of enlightenment within the lotuses. Amitābha Buddha!

With single-minded reverence, I pay homage. In the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, when those from the ten directions gather like clouds and utter words of praise for meditative concentration, [the Buddhas] appear universally before them—the Buddhas of oceans of past kalpas, as numerous as the atoms within all lands.
With single-minded reverence, I pay homage to all the Buddhas as numerous as motes of dust within the Indra-net worlds of the Flower Treasury World.
With single-minded reverence, I pay homage to the Great, Inconceivable, Perfectly Harmonious Dharma Jewel:
the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, the Root Wheel of Dharma, which is vast, expansive, and fully endowed with all things. (Three prostrations.)
With single-minded reverence, I pay homage to the *Kulaputra-sūtra* and other scriptures taught by Śākyamuni, the sūtras as numerous as the atoms within the buddha-fields of the ten directions,
and the entire collection of sūtras comprising all dharma-gates.

With single-minded reverence, I pay homage to Samantabhadra Bodhisattva—the Lord of the Assembly at the site of enlightenment, the primary figure of the Avataṃsaka, and the sovereign of the Buddha-fruit—who, together with all the great Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, has gathered simultaneously throughout the entirety of the Dharma-realm. (Three prostrations.)
With single-minded reverence, I pay homage to the Lord of the Universal Radiance Hall, the presiding host of the Assembly on the Ten Faiths,
the foremost of the Avataṃsaka, Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva, and Bodhisattva Bhadrapāla, who have gathered together like clouds, pervading the entire Dharma-realm,
along with all the great Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas.
With single-minded reverence, I pay homage to the Bodhisattva Dharmamati, Lord of the Assembly of the Ten Abodes in the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven Palace,
who, together with a multitude of great Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, has gathered like clouds, pervading the entire Dharma-realm.
With single-minded reverence, I pay homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Guṇakāraṇḍavyūha, the presiding lord of the tenth assembly in the palace of the Yāma Heaven,
who has gathered together with others throughout the entire realm of phenomena, along with all the great Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas.
With single-minded reverence, I pay homage to Vajradhvaja Bodhisattva, the presiding host of the Assembly of the Ten Dedications in the Tuṣita Heaven Palace,
together with all the great Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas who have gathered like clouds, pervading the entire Dharma-realm.
With single-minded reverence, I pay homage to the Lord of the Palace of Paranirmita-vaśavartin, the Bodhisattva Vimukticandra, the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha,

and all the other great Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas who have gathered together like clouds, pervading the entire Dharma-realm, presiding over the assembly for the Questions and Answers on the Ten Stages.
With single-minded reverence, they pay homage once again at the Hall of Universal Radiance (*Samantāloka-maṇḍala*).

The presiding masters of the stages of Equal Enlightenment (*samyak-saṃbodhi*) and Wondrous Enlightenment (*vibuddha*), including Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, Samantanetra Bodhisattva, Cittarāja Bodhisattva,

Nīlotpalagarbha Bodhisattva, Ratnapāṇi Bodhisattva, and Tathāgatagotra-prabhava-guṇarāja Bodhisattva, gathered together simultaneously, pervading the entire Dharma-realm, along with all the great Bodhisattvas.
To the Mahāsattvas, I pay homage with single-minded reverence. At the Hall of Universal Radiance during the third assembly, the Lord of the Great Practice Assembly, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva,
along with Prajñāgupta Bodhisattva and others, gathered simultaneously in clouds, pervading the entire Dharma-realm— all these great Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas.

Sā. With single-minded reverence, [I pay homage]. In the Jeta Grove, at the original assembly of the Tathāgata, all gathered together like clouds, pervading the entire dharma-realm, were the great Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas.
With single-minded reverence, I pay homage to the Perfectly Enlightened and Wondrous Wisdom, the Universal Teacher of all Buddhas and Patriarchs;

to the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī; and to the fifty-five stages of virtuous spiritual friends throughout the seven locations and nine assemblies of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra, wherein the principal and the associates mutually manifest one another.
I pay single-minded homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas as numerous as motes of dust,
who possess perfect penetration and unimpededness, pervading the ten directions, dwelling on Mount Potalaka, and universally saving all beings through great compassion.
I pay single-minded homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara,
who dwells peacefully within the pavilion adorned by Vairocana; and to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Maitreya, the Compassionate Honored One who is next in succession to Buddhahood.

With single-minded reverence, I pay homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Sudhana, who, at the assembly of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra, resolved his mind upon Bodhi and sought out all the spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*) to the south,
thereby accomplishing the unsurpassed, perfect capacity within a single lifetime.

With single-minded reverence, I pay homage to all the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas of the ten directions and the three periods of time— those who appear from between the eyebrows within the Bodhi tree, upon the lion throne,

amidst the ocean-like assemblies of the *Avataṃsaka* as numerous as the atoms of Buddha-fields, within the realm of the Flower Treasury (*Kusumatalagarbha*), layer upon layer, infinitely and inexhaustibly.
With single-minded reverence, I pay homage to the Śrāvakas such as Śāriputra and the five hundred disciples,
the six thousand bhikṣus, and all the Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, and noble Saṅgha from the Buddha-fields of the ten directions, within the assembly of the final age at the Jeta Grove Monastery.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Vajrapāṇi deities, the deities of the body, the deities of the feet,

the deities of the site of enlightenment, the lords of cities, the lords of the earth, the lords of mountains, the lords of forests, the lords of medicinal herbs, the lords of crops, the lords of rivers,

the lords of oceans, the lords of water, the lords of fire, the lords of wind, the lords of space, the lords of the directions, the lords of night, and the lords of day, as well as the eight classes of beings, including devas and nāgas. Thus it is explained in the Avataṃsaka Sūtra.
Brahmā Deva-rāja, the immeasurable devas, the Sun and Moon Deva-kings, and all the assemblies of holy ones, prostrate themselves before the eternally abiding Triple Gem.
(Recite the Mantra of Universal Prostration silently three times; one should visualize making universal prostrations to all the worthy and holy ones.)

Oṃ. Sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhāna-svabhāva-śuddha-svāhā. (The mantras and mudrās collected here within this ritual for the maṇḍala are the Secret Dharma. In the final age, practitioners have many distracted minds;
without the assistance and protection of secret mantras, it is difficult to achieve success in contemplative practice. After reciting the mantra, chant:)
I, the bhikṣu [Name], with a sincere heart pay homage to all Buddhas.
To all the Lions among Men throughout the worlds of the ten directions and across the three periods of time,
I prostrate with my pure body, speech, and mind, universally and exhaustively, leaving none remaining.
Having paid homage to all Buddhas, I take refuge and pay obeisance to Samantabhadra Bodhisattva and all the Triple Gem. (One prostration and three bows;
hereafter, follow this pattern.)

Second, one praises the Tathāgata (thereby severing the four grave obstacles of speech, attaining the four kinds of unimpeded eloquence, and having a tongue-mark that covers [the face]; endowed with the ten types of perfect vocal resonance).
Having paid homage to the Triple Gem, one kneels on the right knee with palms joined, faces the Dharma seat, and burns incense and scatters flowers.
Visualize the Three Jewels and their subtle, wondrous merits; gaze upon them with undivided devotion. Recite this Brahma-praise:
Bhagavān Vairocana, By the power of your vows, you pervade the entire realm of saṃsāra;
Within all lands, you constantly turn the unsurpassed wheel. A single hair-pore manifests divine transformations, Which all Buddhas proclaim in unison.
Even after passing through immeasurable eons, one cannot reach its limit. (Direct praise:
The physical form of Samantabhadra is like space; Abiding in reality, it is not a land.
According to the desires of the minds of all sentient beings, He manifests his universal body, equal to all.
The virtues of the Bodhisattva are boundless; All sublime practices are fully perfected.
Even if immeasurable and infinite Buddhas Were to speak for immeasurable eons, they could not exhaust them.
(When the praise is concluded, the presiding master says:)
I, Bhikṣu [Name], with a sincere heart, praise the Tathāgata.
With an ocean of all vocal sounds, universally producing inexhaustible and wondrous words and phrases throughout all future kalpas, I praise the Buddha’s profoundly deep ocean of merit.
Having praised the Tathāgata, I take refuge in and pay homage to Samantabhadra Bodhisattva and all the Triple Gem. (Perform one prostration and three bows, then stand and say:)

(Strike the chime) I, Bhikṣu [Name], on this day and at this hour of the night, through the roots of goodness obtained from this offering of praise and worship, dedicate them to the ocean of sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm.
May they all forever be free from the hindrances and obscurations, and may they accomplish the path of the Knowledge of All Modes.
Third, extensively cultivating offerings (removes the obstacle of stinginess and greed; the various sages are delighted; the presiding master says):

All these members of the assembly kneel on their right knees, solemnly holding incense and flowers, making offerings according to the Dharma throughout the entire Lotus Treasury World and within the Indra-net lands to the Three Jewels of perfect fusion and unimpededness.
(At this point, stop chanting. Holding the flowers with the hands, one should give rise to contemplative practice in accordance with the sutra.)

The Cloud of Silent Contemplation says: Within every single atom of all Buddha-lands throughout the entirety of the Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space, across the ten directions and the three periods of time, there is, in each and every atom, a number of Buddhas equal to the atoms within all worlds; and at the site of each and every such Buddha...

Surrounded by an ocean-like assembly of various bodhisattvas, through the power of my vows and conduct as Samantabhadra, I give rise to profound faith and understanding, perceiving them directly before me. I offer all manner of sublime and excellent offerings, namely:

clouds of flowers, clouds of garlands, clouds of celestial music, clouds of celestial parasols, clouds of celestial garments, and clouds of various celestial perfumes—unguents, incense for burning, and powdered incense—each cloud as vast in measure as Sumeru, the king of mountains; and I light various kinds of lamps.

[Visualize] lamps made of the aggregates (*skandha*), lamps of various fragrant oils; each lamp-wick is like Mount Sumeru, and the oil for each lamp is like the waters of the great ocean. Constantly making offerings with such articles of worship, having visualized this, scatter flowers and chant:
May these clouds of incense and flowers pervade the Lotus Treasury World and within the lands of Indra’s net; through the power of Samantabhadra’s vows, may they all become Dharma offerings.

May these offerings fill all of space and pervade the entire Dharma realm—within every single atom of all Buddha-fields throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time—to the Buddhas as numerous as the atoms therein, and at each and every Buddha’s place, to the inconceivable ocean-like assemblies.
There were everywhere various sublime clouds of incense, fragrant oils, incense lamps, flower garlands, necklaces, parasols, music, banners, jeweled canopies, robes, and food and drink—
vast offerings that constantly performed the work of the Buddha, universally perfuming all sentient beings.

Generating the Bodhicitta (Next, form the Great Amoghasiddhi-maṇi mudrā: join the two hands in the vajra-añjali; curve the two index fingers into the shape of a jewel; extend the two thumbs side by side.
Recite the Amoghapāśa Maṇi Offering Dhāraṇī. The presiding master shall say:)
Oṃ āḥ māṃ padme bhagavati mātṛke tathāgate mīlaṅkīti sarvamantraprasara hūṃ. (Recite this three times silently.
One should visualize that throughout the entire dharma-realm of space, there are divine, wondrous incenses, flowers, and all manner of offerings.)
Cloud-seas and so forth fill the entirety of space. With a sincere heart, one makes offerings to the Triple Gem. Having completed the visualization, one says:
"I, the bhikṣu [Name], with a sincere heart, extensively cultivate these offerings."
With the most excellent and wonderful flower garlands, Music, ointments, and parasols—
With such supreme articles of adornment, I make offerings to all the Tathāgatas.
With the most excellent garments and the finest perfumes, Powdered incense, burning incense, and lamps and candles.
Each one like a heap of Mount Sumeru; I have made offerings to all the Tathāgatas.
Having extensively performed these offerings, I take refuge in and pay homage to Samantabhadra Bodhisattva and the Triple Gem.

(One prostration) Fourth, the Repentance of Karmic Obstructions (to sever the four obstructions and ten obstacles, to accomplish all mundane and supramundane merits, and to obtain an excellent primary and secondary retribution).
(The offerings having been completed, one kneels upright before the Dharma seat with the right knee touching the ground,

burning incense and scattering flowers while visualizing the Three Jewels filling the vast expanse of space, surrounded by the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra and his immeasurable, magnificently adorned retinue.)

Acting as the presiding master of the confession, next visualize and say: "For all the karmic obstacles of every sin committed by myself and all sentient beings since beginningless time, I pray that the Triple Gem will take pity and deliver us.
May our deluded karma be instantly dispelled and transformed into pure causes. May body and mind together become empty, and may sins and merits be found to have no master.
May we clearly perceive true nature, which is equal to the Dharma-body of the Buddhas, and may the transgressions of the three karmas be perfected as the three liberations."
To be liberated from the heavy obstructions of the six sense faculties and transform them into the six supernormal powers—having thus contemplated, he raises his voice and says):
"Universally for the four debts of gratitude, the three realms of existence, and all sentient beings of the Dharma realm, may all obstructions be severed and eliminated. I take refuge and repent."

(Having finished chanting, rise and perform one prostration. Again, kneel with the right knee on the ground and join the palms. Contemplate the ten minds in both forward and reverse order, silently reciting the *Qingliang Gāthā*:
(Since beginningless time I have given rise to ignorance, And encountered evil friends who increased my afflictions.)
Lacking a mind of sympathetic joy, one’s virtue is forever extinguished; Though physical, verbal, and mental evils gradually arise, the mind pervades everywhere, defiling every point of contact.
From thought to thought they continue in succession, busying themselves day and night;
They do not wish for others to know, concealing their own transgressions. Fearless of the evil realms, they act with unrestrained license.
Lack of shame and lack of remorse are the nets of Māra; Denying cause and denying effect is the pit of icchantikas.
Having thus followed the current and turned one's back on the source, The ocean of birth-and-death suffering remains vast and full.
Fortunately, you recognize the Son of the Tathāgata, the Elder; Now you wish to go against the current and abandon the village of poverty.
Right faith in cause and effect destroys the icchantika; shame and remorse destroy the shameless.
Fear of the miserable realms destroys fearlessness; the disclosure of sinful karma destroys concealment.
Severing the mind of continuity destroys constant recollection; the arousal of the bodhicitta destroys pervasive arising.
Cultivating merit to remedy faults breaks indulgence; Guarding the True Dharma breaks thoughts of lack of joy;
The Buddhas of the Ten Directions break evil associates; Contemplating the emptiness of the nature of offenses breaks the fetters.
(Venerably, I pray that the Buddhas of the Ten Directions, the World-Honored One Vairocana, and Samantabhadra Bodhisattva will compassionately accept me. Having thus visualized:
(Recite: With a sincere heart, I repent. Bhikṣu [Name], I take refuge in the inexhaustible Triple Gem of the ten directions. May you arise with compassion for me.

To serve as clear testimony: I, the Dharma-realm, and all sentient beings, since the beginningless kalpas of the past, have, due to greed, hatred, and delusion, produced various evil karmas through body, speech, and mind; our eyes have been deluded by forms, becoming stained with attachment to dark and bright colors.
Red, green, crimson, and purple; rare curiosities and precious ornaments; various bodily forms—long or short, black or white; the characteristics of their postures; the ears craving pleasant sounds:
the notes of the *gong* and *shang*, stringed instruments and pipes, the music of performance and song, the sounds of speech and language, and the expressions of weeping and laughter.

The nose relies upon fragrant incense: musk, deep-fragrant orchids, turmeric, and storax. The tongue craves exquisite flavors: fresh lambs, sweet and fatty meats, and the flesh and blood of sentient beings.
These nourish the four great elements, yet they constantly increase the root of suffering. The body delights in finery: brocades, embroideries, silks, and fine gauzes.
All fine textures and the seven precious, beautiful garments cause my mind to be filled with many distracting thoughts; every touch is contrary to my peace.

These six faculties of mine are shrouded by ignorance, leading me to commit endless sins, obstructing the causes for the Buddha-dharma, opening the path for the icchantikas, and turning my back on the intent of the Sages.
Following after evil conditions, they abandon bodhicitta and indulge in the cycle of birth and death; regarding the dharma of renunciation, they lack even a single thought of it.
For a long night, they have accumulated the causes of all bitter poisons, defiling those beyond training (aśaikṣa), as well as their kin and non-kin, and even renunciants.
They beat, revile, and scold others; they associate with those of evil dharma; they defile stupas and monasteries; they violate their precepts and vows;

they indulge their bodies and minds in dissipation; they envy virtuous people; they rebel against and harm their teachers and elders; their greed and anger are fierce and intense; they show no regard for kindness or enmity; and the poison of ignorance deludes their hearts.

How could they know when to advance or retreat? They have unjustly executed the innocent and indiscriminately harmed the virtuous and good. Their greedy desires never cease; they employ a thousand kinds of deceitful schemes.

Though their worldly ambitions are fully satisfied, they employ a hundred forms of fraud and hypocrisy. In every way they encroach upon and deceive others, taking the false for the real, and they are addicted to wine and sensual pleasures.
Making no distinction between enemies and kin, they engage in empty, deceptive, and false speech, causing immense harm.

They deceive their six relations, fail in filial piety toward their parents, give rise to various heterodox views, slander the sages and saints, and treat the Triple Gem with contempt. Possessing craving and delusion, they lack both shame and remorse.
Through the six sense organs and three types of action, we have committed every kind of transgression, from the most grave to the lightest; these obstacles of sin are immeasurable and boundless.
If these evil karmas possessed physical form or characteristics, even the entirety of the realm of empty space could not contain them.

We reflect upon our own meager virtues, whose retribution lies within the human condition, and are fortunate to have encountered the Tathāgata’s Great Flower Adornment Sūtra, which perfects the wheel of causes. Relying upon this—

Dharma Gate: The Practice of the Method of Repentance. Now, with my three karmas entirely purified, I universally repent before all the Buddhas and assemblies of Bodhisattvas throughout the entire Dharma-realm and within every most minute atom of lands, with a sincere heart, never to create such [karma] again, and to dwell constantly in pure precepts and all meritorious virtues.
I pray only that the Honored One Vairocana and the Repentance Master Samantabhadra...
May the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, and the inexhaustible Triple Gem of the Flower Adornment Ocean Assembly take pity upon us and protect us with mindfulness.

May the sun of wisdom shed its light to dissolve the frost and dew of karmic afflictions within our bodies and minds; may the wind of compassion blow universally to shatter the mountains of heavy obstructions.
May the water of the Dharma flow forever, washing away the defilements of my mind; may it overturn the three poisons and transform them into the three secret treasuries.

May I universally bestow this upon all sentient beings, so that they may all ascend to the realm of truth and, like Sudhana, achieve the ten great kings of vows of Samantabhadra within a single lifetime.
I pay homage to all Buddhas. I praise the Tathāgatas. I extensively cultivate offerings. I repent of karmic obstructions. I rejoice in all merits.

I entreat the turning of the Wheel of Dharma. I entreat the Buddhas to remain in the world. I constantly follow and learn from the Buddhas. I always accord with the needs of sentient beings. I universally dedicate all these merits.
Throughout the expanse of space and the realm of phenomena, for all infinite sentient beings, may they always attain peace and happiness; may they be free from all illness and suffering;
may all attempts to commit unwholesome deeds fail to be accomplished; may all cultivated roots of goodness swiftly reach fulfillment; and may all [evil paths] be closed off.
I shall open the gates to all evil realms and reveal to humans and devas the correct path to nirvāṇa.

If there are sentient beings who, due to the accumulation of various evil karmas, experience all manner of most grievous fruits of suffering, I shall undergo them all in their stead, so that those sentient beings may [be freed].

They shall all attain liberation and ultimately achieve unsurpassed bodhi. Able to rescue and deliver sentient beings from the great ocean of afflictions and suffering, causing them to escape and all attain rebirth in the Land of Ultimate Bliss of Amitābha Buddha.

(Once the offenses have been confessed, next perform the seal for repentance that extinguishes transgressions. Form the Vajra-bond with both hands. The six fingers are positioned outward like human hands;
bend the second joints of the thumbs and forefingers; press the ring fingers and little fingers over the two middle fingers. Recite the secret mantra of repentance.)
Oṃ sarvabuddhabodhisattvapādamūle namo namo dharmāya svāhā. (Recite this silently once.
One should visualize that before each and every Buddha, one’s own body is present, seeking mercy and repenting. Having completed the visualization, recite aloud:)
I, Bhikṣu [Name], with a sincere heart, repent of my karmic obstructions.
All the various evil karmas I have created in the past, arising from the body, speech,
and mind due to beginningless greed, hatred, and delusion— I now repent of them all.
Having finished repenting for karmic obstructions, take refuge and pay homage to Samantabhadra Bodhisattva and all the Triple Gem. (One prostration.

Fifth is the merit of sympathetic joy (*anumodana*). This eliminates obstacles such as a lack of delight in the prosperity of others and jealousy; it secures immeasurable blessings, gives rise to impartial goodness, and results in obtaining a great retinue.
All merits are entirely perfected).
I, the bhikṣu [Name], with a sincere heart, rejoice in these merits.
May all sentient beings throughout the ten directions—the followers of the two vehicles, both those in training and those beyond training—[attain them].
I rejoice in all the merits of all Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas.
Having rejoiced in these merits, I take refuge in and pay homage to the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra and the Three Jewels. (One prostration) Sixth, the Request to Turn the Wheel of Dharma:

(This eliminates obstacles such as violating the Dharma and slandering the teachings; it gives rise to the roots of goodness of loving-kindness and compassion; and one attains the uncommon merit of extensive learning, hearing, and wisdom. [In contrast,] the Śrāvakas seek only their own liberation.)

I merely perform repentance. However, out of compassion for others, a bodhisattva must exhort all Buddhas to universally rain down the rain of Dharma so that both self and others may be thoroughly moistened.
I, the bhikṣu [Name], with a sincere heart, entreat you to turn the wheel of Dharma.
I now exhort all the Lamps of the World throughout the ten directions, those who first achieved enlightenment, to turn the supreme, wondrous Wheel of Dharma.
Having requested them to turn the Wheel of Dharma, I take refuge in and pay homage to the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra and all the Triple Gem. (One prostration)

Seventh is requesting the Buddha to remain in the world (which eliminates the obstacles of slandering the Sangha, the Buddha, or harming the Buddha, as well as hating and envying Bodhisattvas and spiritual friends who do not wish for him to remain in the world, thereby attaining an indestructible vajra body).
I, the bhikṣu [Name], with a sincere heart, entreat all Buddhas to remain in the world.
Should any Buddha wish to manifest parinirvāṇa, I shall with utmost sincerity exhort them,
praying that they remain for as many eons as there are atoms in a buddha-field, for the benefit and happiness of all sentient beings.
Having requested the Buddha to remain in the world, take refuge and pay homage to Samantabhadra Bodhisattva and all the Triple Gem. (One prostration.

Eighth, Constantly Following the Buddha’s Example: (This eliminates obstacles such as contravening the Buddha and spiritual friends, the failure to accumulate merit, the lack of resolve for cultivation, and the failure to benefit both oneself and others;
it leads to the attainment of the inexhaustible merits of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.)
I, the bhikṣu [Name], with a sincere heart, constantly follow and learn from the Buddha.
I follow all Tathāgatas in my learning, cultivating the perfect conduct of Samantabhadra,
making offerings to all the Tathāgatas of the past and the Buddhas of the present throughout the ten directions.

The future teachers of all devas and humans, Whose every aspiration is perfectly fulfilled— I vow to follow their training throughout the three periods of time, And swiftly attain the great enlightenment of Bodhi.
Having thus followed the Buddha’s training, I take refuge in and pay homage to the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra and all the Triple Gem. (One prostration)

Ninth, always acting in accordance with sentient beings (severing the various dispositions of sentient beings—whether they appear as enemies or friends, or whether they are compliant or antagonistic—and being unable to follow them; this displeases the Buddha and constitutes an obstacle equal to violating the Buddha;
by doing so, one obtains vast spiritual benefactors as one's retinue).
I, the bhikṣu [Name], with a sincere heart, always accord with sentient beings.
I constantly follow and comply with all sentient beings, and throughout all future kalpas,
I shall eternally cultivate the vast vows of Samantabhadra to fulfill unsurpassed, great Bodhi.
Having thus constantly conformed to the needs of sentient beings, I take refuge in and pay homage to Samantabhadra Bodhisattva and all the Triple Gem. (One prostration.
Tenth: Universal Dedication (which severs the obstacle of not generating the bodhicitta, brings the perfection of the ten pāramitās, and results in the attainment of the ten bodies).
All merit from prostrations, praises, and offerings, The request for the Buddhas to remain and turn the wheel of Dharma,
Rejoicing, repentance, and all roots of goodness— I dedicate them to sentient beings and the path of Buddhahood.
This sublime practice of Samantabhadra, And its boundless, supreme merit, I dedicate in full.
May all sentient beings drowning in the sea of suffering Swiftly proceed to the realm of Amitābha Buddha.
Having universally dedicated [the merit], take refuge in Samantabhadra Bodhisattva and all the Triple Gem. (One prostration) The Ninth:

Circumambulation and Recitation of the Sūtra. (Having completed the dedication, straighten your posture with dignified deportment and stand still for a moment. You should visualize that the Triple Gem and the Sage [Samantabhadra] fill the void of space, each seated upon their Dharma throne.)
Afterward, he burned various kinds of incense and saw his own body circumambulating the Dharma seat one by one, walking with calm composure and slow steps, while reciting:
"Namo to the Buddhas of the ten directions;
Namo to the Dharma of the ten directions."
Namo to the Sangha of the Ten Directions. (Chant "He Fan," circumambulate, and hold the incense burner horizontally at the level of the eyebrows.
Namo to Vairocana Buddha. Namo to Amitābha Buddha.
Homage to all Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in the Flower Treasury World.
Homage to the Great Vaipulya Buddhāvataṃsaka Sūtra.
Homage to Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
Homage to Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva.
Homage to Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
Homage to Maitreya Bodhisattva.
Homage to Bodhisattva Sudhana;
homage to the great Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas of the Avataṃsaka Ocean Assembly (recite three times). [Afterwards, perform the inquiry of well-being.
(Now, as for circumambulation: it is an expression of longing and devotion for the subtle and wondrous merits of the Triple Gem. Thus one performs three circuits, up to seven.)
[One should circumambulate] seven hundred times, though there is no fixed number. Once the names of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas have been recited, the presiding master announces:
"The *Avataṃsaka-sūtra*, the *Chapter on the Vows and Practices of Samantabhadra Entering the Inconceivable Realm of Liberation*," and so forth.
Once the scripture has been thus announced, one again recites the names of the Three Jewels once. Thereafter, one proceeds to the front of the Dharma seat.
With single-minded right mindfulness, chant the Three Refuges:
I take refuge in the Buddha; may all sentient beings realize the Great Way and give rise to the unsurpassed mind.
I take refuge in the Dharma; may all sentient beings enter deeply into the treasury of the scriptures, their wisdom as vast as the ocean.
Taking refuge in the Sangha, may all beings govern the great assemblies with complete unimpededness. *Vandana* to the noble assembly. (The Three Refuges are concluded.

Then, mentally taking refuge in Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, exit by circling to the right. Arrive at the meditation hall and take your place in the ranks; recite the four lines beginning with "The four modes of birth and the nine realms of existence," etc.)

Section Ten: Sitting Upright in Contemplation (Based on the practice of the Perfect Teaching, this is briefly divided into two parts. First is the realization of the *Vairocana* Dharma-realm, as taught in the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*.
This refers to the single, true, and unobstructed Dharma-realm, also termed the "One Mind," within which the three worlds and the four dharmas are inherently complete.)
The Dharmadhātu. Among all dharmas, whether defiled or pure, not a single dharma exists outside of this Dharmadhātu.

This is the true mind that serves as the fundamental basis for all ordinary beings and those who have passed through the stages of cultivation. Generally speaking, there are two types: first, the true mind of the Common Teaching;

second, the true mind of the Distinct Teaching. Within the [Common] Teaching, there are further two: first, the true mind of the Final Teaching, which is what the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* states: "One should know..."
Space arises within your mind, like a fragment of cloud appearing in the vast clarity of the great sky; how much more so, then, do all worlds exist within space? It is further said:
"Space arises within the Great Enlightenment, like a single bubble emerging from the sea. The minute dust-motes of all contaminated lands are all produced in dependence upon space. It is also said:
"The true mind is omnipresent and perfect, encompassing and enveloping the ten directions. Look back at that which was born of your parents—"
This body is like a single mote of dust blown within the void of the ten directions, existing yet as if non-existent. Furthermore, it is said:
"All things that exist within all worlds are none other than the wondrous, luminous true mind of Bodhi. All sentient beings..."
Since beginningless time, one has been deluded regarding this mind, falsely identifying the four elements as the body and discursive thoughts as the mind.
It is like failing to recognize hundreds of thousands of clear, vast oceans, while instead recognizing only a single floating bubble.

Second, the True Mind of the Sudden Teaching is described as all-pervading and pure, leaving no room for anything else within it; all delusive thoughts are fundamentally non-existent, being the absolute, unconditioned reality.
The mind is fundamentally pure. The *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* states: "The nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is originally empty and quiescent;
there is neither grasping nor seeing. This emptiness of nature is itself the Buddha; it cannot be conceived or measured. The *Śraddhotpāda Śāstra* states:
"All phenomena, from the very beginning, are free from characteristics such as verbal expression; they are ultimately equal, without change, indestructible, and are solely this one [reality]."

Because it is the mind, it is called True Suchness (*tathatā*). This refers to the aforementioned Final Teaching (*paryantavāda*), which, in accordance with the delusions of sentient beings, speaks of the existence of physical bodies, mountains, rivers, the great earth, and all worldly phenomena, so as to cause sentient beings to overturn delusion and return to the True.

Through this, they realize that physical bodies, mountains, rivers, the great earth, and so forth, are entirely the single-flavored, wondrously luminous true mind. Now, within the Sudden Teaching (*tatkṣaṇavāda*), there is fundamentally no physical body, mountains, or great earth.
The Ground is, fundamentally, the single-flavored, non-contingent true mind. Thus, Qingliang said: "In total, no dharmic characteristics are taught;
only the true nature is discerned. Bodhidharma said: "My Dharma transmits the mind by means of the mind, without establishing written words. This refers precisely to the transmission of this mind.
Caodong (Caoqi) said: "The bright mirror is fundamentally pure; why rely on wiping away dust? This, too, refers to this very mind.
Second, the one mind of the Separate Teaching refers to the one true, unobstructed Great Dharma-realm mind. It encompasses the three worlds and possesses the four dharma-realms;
it is entirely this and entirely that, without any obstruction. Within this one true Great Dharma-realm, whether ordinary person or...
O Sage, whether it be principle or phenomenon, whichever single dharma is raised, it is entirely the Great Dharma-realm Mind.

Even if one raises but a single mote of dust, that too is entirely the Great Dharma-realm Mind. As the Sūtra says: "In the Flower Treasury World, within every single mote of dust, the Dharma-realm is seen.
Furthermore, since this single mote of dust is the Great Dharma-realm Mind, within this single mote of dust, the Great Dharma...
Within the realm, if one were to further take up even a single atom, it would likewise be entirely the mind of the Great Dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu-citta*).

Whether taken horizontally or vertically, as one takes them up layer upon layer, there are layer upon layer of Dharma-realms. Therefore, Master Qingliang, in his commentary on the "Ten Stages" chapter (*Daśabhūmika-sūtra-śāstra*), spoke of the inexhaustible single mind of the Indra-net (*indrājāla*).
Since beginningless time, all sentient beings have been deluded and ignorant of this inexhaustible Dharma-realm.
This is one's own body and mind, within which are inherently present the inexhaustible qualities of form and mind like an Indra’s net (indrajāla), equal in stature to the body and mind of Vairocana.
Yet, one mistakenly clings to this unobstructed Buddha-body and Buddha-mind of one's own house as being a defiled sentient being.
It is, for example, like a Wheel-Turning Sage King who governs the four continents, fully endowed with both physical majesty and wisdom, and possessed of great wealth.

In incomparable bliss, he suddenly fell into a deep sleep and dreamed that he was an ant. Within the state of that dream, he recognized only himself as an ant, unaware that he was originally a universal monarch (*cakravartin*).
Therefore, if one seeks to achieve the ultimate fruit of Buddhahood, it is essential to awaken to this *Vairocana* dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*).
If one has not awakened to this dharma-realm, even if one practices the myriad deeds for many eons, it will all be in vain.
To merely undergo toil and hardship cannot be called being a true Bodhisattva.

(2) Cultivating the Ocean of Samantabhadra’s Practices: Having already attained realization of the unobstructed Dharma-realm within one's own mind, one possesses therein the primary marks and secondary signs as numerous as the atoms in ten lotus-treasury worlds, along with the inexhaustible supernatural powers and merits of the Indra-net. With these—
The Buddhas of the ten directions are no different from one another. Yet, because we have been bound by deluded attachments since beginningless time, these habits have become our very nature;
it is difficult to exhaust them all at once. Consequently, we are unable to freely enjoy the spiritual powers and merits that belong to us.

Therefore, one must accord with the *dharmadhātu* of one’s own *tathāgata-garbha*, cultivating the ocean of the primordially present practices of Samantabhadra, so that this inexhaustible function may swiftly [be realized].
Because this is attained through direct manifestation, the Sūtra says: "Those who cultivate this Dharma require little effort and will swiftly attain Bodhi.
Now, regarding contemplative practice (*vipaśyanā*), two gates will be briefly shown. The first is the Contemplation of the Inexhaustible Indra-Net. Within this, five further gates are opened.

The first is the Gate of Prostration and Reverence, which means visualizing that throughout the entirety of empty space and the pervasive Dharma-realm, in every atom and every land, there are inexhaustible Three Jewels like an Indra-net.
Before each [of these], there are infinite bodies like a celestial net (*jāla-netra*). Within each single body, one pays homage before each of the infinite Three Jewels like a celestial net.
Before each and every Jewel, there are again infinite bodies like a celestial net performing prostrations.

One should further contemplate this single gateway as continuing without rest until the end of the future, with mindfulness succeeding mindfulness in an uninterrupted succession, such that the actions of body, speech, and mind are never-ceasing.
(There is weariness and fatigue).

(2) The Gate of Making Offerings: This refers to the visualization that throughout the entirety of space and the Dharma-realm, in every atom and every buddha-field, before each of the inexhaustible Three Jewels—which are like Indra’s net—there is an equally inexhaustible body of one's own, also like Indra’s net;
and from each and every one of these bodies, there issues forth an inexhaustible Indra’s net...

Exhaustively providing all offerings—namely, incense, flowers, lamps and candles, robes, food and drink, banners and pennants, parasols, canopies, clouds of necklaces, and so forth—each of these produced offerings is individually offered to the inexhaustible Three Jewels of the Indra-net. Before each and every Jewel, [one offers].
Each possesses an inexhaustible body like a celestial net (jāla-netra) for making offerings, continuing from thought-moment to thought-moment without interruption, their physical, verbal,
and mental actions never wearying or becoming exhausted.

(Third, the Gate of Repentance: This means to contemplate that throughout the entirety of empty space and the pervasive Dharma-realm, in every atom and every buddha-field, before each of the inexhaustible Three Jewels—as vast as an Indra’s net—there is an equally inexhaustible body, like an Indra’s net; and with each and every such body, one performs repentance with the utmost sincerity.)
Regarding the inexhaustible web-of-Indra-like offenses and obscurations— namely, the five heinous crimes, the ten non-virtues, and so forth,

as well as the afflictive and cognitive obscurations committed from beginningless time until the present life— for each and every such offense and obscuration, there is an inexhaustible body of confession like a web-of-Indra.
This continues moment to moment in uninterrupted succession, with no weariness or fatigue in the actions of body, speech, and mind.

The fourth is the gate of making vows, which means: contemplating that throughout the entirety of space and the pervasive Dharma-realm, in every atom and every land, before each of the inexhaustible Three Jewels as vast as an Indra’s net, there is a body as inexhaustible as an Indra’s net; and from each and every body, one makes vows as inexhaustible as an Indra’s net, namely:
"I vow to deliver boundless sentient beings; I vow to sever boundless afflictions; I vow to [venerate] boundless Buddhas..."
One should vow to study the Dharma; vow to accumulate boundless merit and wisdom; and vow to realize unsurpassed bodhi.

Furthermore, one should fully give rise to all the virtuous vows that one’s own heart delights in. Each and every such vow is further manifested through bodies as infinite as a celestial net (*jāla-netra*), continuing from moment to moment without interruption. In these activities of body, speech, and mind, there shall be no weariness or fatigue.

(5) The Gate of Recitation: This refers to visualizing that throughout the entirety of space, pervading the Dharma-realm, within every atom and every buddha-field, before each of the infinite Three Jewels as vast as an Indra’s net, there exists an infinite body as vast as an Indra’s net.
Within each and every body, one recites the names of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas from the infinite teachings as vast as an Indra’s net.
Within each and every name of a Buddha or Bodhisattva from those infinite teachings...
The Emperor’s Net of Infinite Bodies is maintained, with every thought-moment succeeding one another without interruption;
in body, speech, and mind, there is no weariness or fatigue. Regarding these five preceding gates:

whether one performs this visualization while seated, or during times of prostration and making offerings, one enters each respective visualization and briefly collects the mind. The merit is inexhaustible. Qingliang said: "If one does not enter..."
This contemplation merely exhausts oneself in vain.
(2) The Contemplation of the Unobstructed Dharma-realm: This means constantly perceiving all phenomena, whether defiled or pure, as being in their entirety the mind of the unobstructed Dharma-realm.
One should likewise perceive this contemplating wisdom as being entirely the mind of the Dharma-realm. As the sutra says:
It is said: "To know that all phenomena are the very nature of the mind is to accomplish the body of wisdom, which is not realized through another.
Furthermore, Qingliang (Chengguan) said: "If one knows that whatever is encountered is the mind, only then does one fully understand the nature of the mind.

Now, within this unobstructed *dharmadhātu*, the three worlds, the four *dharmadhātus*, and all phenomena—both defiled and pure—are inherently complete; this *dharmadhātu* is entirely this, and entirely that.
When these are mutually unobstructed, one knows that every faculty (*indriya*) and every object (*viṣaya*) is entirely the unobstructed Dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*).

If, within the four modes of deportment, one constantly contemplates that both faculties and objects are all the infinitely layered and inexhaustible Dharma-realm, one is practicing the sphere of Samantabhadra.
This contemplation is the root of all samādhi-gates; if one practices it constantly, then [one attains] the One.
All samādhis will spontaneously manifest before them).
Furthermore, for those who practice the cultivation of the mind, there may arise various dreams of good or evil; they may encounter various demonic obstacles;
various signs of adversity or favor may appear; various sounds of good or evil may be heard; or various insects and ants may infest their bodies.
Whether walking, or when the body and mind are uneasy, or when there is much discursive thought and deliberation,

or when the appearances that arise during meditative observation do not correspond to the primary object of contemplation, one must observe them all as being like a dream or a magical illusion— entirely unreal.
Furthermore, one contemplates that all things arise as manifestations of one's own mind. Thus, the *Śraddhotpāda Śāstra* states: "One should maintain the mindfulness that [all] is but mind;
then objective realms will cease, and one will ultimately not be afflicted by them."
